speeches.speaker: Mark Dreyfus
speeches.brief: Introduced the Privacy Amendment (Privacy Alerts) Bill 2013 to require agencies and businesses to notify individuals and the Privacy Commissioner after serious data breaches, a reform recommended by the Australian Law Reform Commission in 2008, citing a February breach that exposed the personal details of almost 50,000 ABC website users.

speeches.speaker: Michael Keenan
speeches.brief: Supported the Privacy Amendment (Privacy Alerts) Bill 2013 requiring mandatory data breach notification, citing the 2011 hack of 77 million Sony PlayStation Network accounts and the 2013 breach exposing almost 50,000 people's details on the ABC website, but reserved the right to amend the bill, set to commence 12 March 2014, pending a Senate committee report due 24 June.

speeches.speaker: Michelle Rowland
speeches.brief: Argued for the Privacy Amendment (Privacy Alerts) Bill 2013, citing Privacy Commissioner Timothy Pilgrim's concern that only 46 data breach notifications were received in 2011-12, an 18 per cent decrease on the previous year despite a rising trend in breaches, and noted a Telstra customer data breach discovered via a Google search on 16 May.

speeches.speaker: Steve Georganas
speeches.brief: Argued for the Privacy Amendment (Privacy Alerts) Bill 2013, recalling Labor first legislated privacy protections in 1988, citing the ABC website hack and Sony's PlayStation Network breach as examples of why mandatory data-breach notification is needed, and explained it would let consumers act quickly, such as cancelling a credit card, once notified.

speeches.speaker: Mark Dreyfus
speeches.brief: Summing up debate on the Privacy Amendment (Privacy Alerts) Bill 2013, cited support from Microsoft, the Office of the Australian Information Commissioner and consumer group Choice, argued Australia's voluntary reporting system is not working given underreporting of breaches, and noted New Zealand, the United States, Canada and the European Union are introducing similar mandatory data-breach laws.
